questions: Does line_loss_events fall below 1 per run, and does max_error move above or below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend?
Does steering_oscillation rise on the slalom compared with the 15 mm spacing at lead 0.07 m (about 0.149)? If so, is the coarser 20 mm spacing causing a less linear signal near centre?
Do the outer sensors at ±0.04 m ever read zero while the robot is on track, or is the signal still monotonic across the row?

Is the remaining failure now limited by the controller (gain or base speed) rather than sensing? If sensing is no longer binding, which geometry lever should move next: wheel_radius for speed, or sensor_size?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If the slalom oscillates heavily at 20 mm spacing, suggest a spacing between 15 and 20 mm (for example 17 mm) at lead 0.07 m. If the oval improves but the s-bend still ends at the same progress, state whether wheel_radius should increase for more ground speed per wheel rotation.

intent: Test whether widening the sensor row from 60 mm to 80 mm span (20 mm spacing, outer sensors at ±0.04 m) extends line capture past the 0.0485 m point where the current row loses the tape. Only sensor spacing changes from iteration 2, where lead 0.07 m was the best measured; drivetrain and body stay the same so the effect is isolated. Expected result: line_loss_events and max_error fall on the oval and s-bend, progress rises on all three tracks, and steering_oscillation on the slalom stays near 0.15 or lower.
learning: Lead has saturated at about 0.07 m: 0.08 m was flat or slightly worse than 0.07 m. Span of the sensor row, which sets the lateral capture limit, is the next untested sensing lever. Track, mass, body and sensor size have shown little effect so far.
rationale: Evidence across four iterations: every development run ends off track at 11-16% progress, with max_error near 0.06 m. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), so the 0.06 m floor binds and body width cannot relax it. Drivetrain changes (track 0.12 to 0.10 m, mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg) moved the score by only 0.14. Moving sensor lead from y=0.05 to 0.07 m raised the score from 52.3 to 60.4, mostly on the oval. Lead 0.08 m gave 60.33, slightly worse than 0.07 m, with the slalom down about 0.18 and the oval flat. So lead has saturated near 0.07 m and further lead gains are not available. The remaining candidate is sensor span. The outer sensors at x=±0.03 m with 12 mm footprints can only see tape when the robot's centre offset is less than about 0.03 + 0.0125 + 0.006 = 0.0485 m. Runs that reach max_error 0.06 m therefore have no tape under any sensor, which fits the single line-loss event per run. I change only the lateral spacing: 20 mm instead of 15 mm, giving x = ±0.04 and ±0.02 m, at y = 0.07 m (the best measured lead). This extends capture to about 0.0605 m, which is just past the off-track limit. Wheels, mass, track, body and sensor size stay fixed, so the result isolates span. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, lower max_error on the oval and s-bend, and more progress. Risk: coarser spacing gives a less linear signal near centre, which may raise steering_oscillation on the slalom. If the oval improves but the slalom oscillates, the next step is to narrow spacing to about 17 mm or raise sensor_size to 0.016 mm rather than move the lead.
